title: OpenAI dots inspire open source imitators amid technical difficulties
key_facts: OpenAI's dots are always-on agents that run in their own cloud computers; The Register reports that multiple users now report task failures and connection issues.
Other reported problems: cloud connectivity, dots that disappear, and refusals that appear tied to abuse prevention; the OpenAI Developer Community forum shows similar complaints.
OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment.

Open-source copies: OpenDots from Tawkit, which makes the CopilotKit toolkit (released in a post the week before), and Open Dot, built by Prathit Joshi, a growth engineer at Composio, which can use open models such as DeepSeek through OpenRouter.
ABI Research, a market research firm, argues 'AI claws' (always-on agents) will shape enterprise AI adoption.
The Register says OpenAI introduced dots 'last month'; yesterday's pool dates OpenAI's dots coverage to 4 to 5 Oct 2026 (WSJ 4 Oct, Moneycontrol 5 Oct).
quote_evidence: Presently, multiple users are reporting task failures and connection issues with their dots.
OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment about the usage of dots.
why_it_matters_hint: People weighing always-on agents; the failure reports come from users and forums, not OpenAI.
event_date: 4 Oct 2026 (earliest yesterday-pool coverage; The Register says 'last month')
